meta.homeowner_title: Get a price for your EV charger
meta.homeowner_intro: Nine questions, about two minutes, and a real price at the end — not a call-back. We honour whatever this gives you.

options.label: On the outside wall of the garage
In a carport, or on the driveway
In a detached garage or shop
At a parking spot away from the house

ask.question: Where do you want the charger?
ask.help: Think about where the car actually sits, and which side the charge port is on. Most chargers come with a cable around 18 to 25 feet.
ask.why: Inside a garage is the simplest and cheapest case. Anything outdoors needs weatherproof parts, and anything in a separate building usually means digging.

states.explain: Lets the shared wire-run questions know whether to ask about weather and digging, without the fragment having to know anything about EV chargers.

options.label: Normal — full overnight
options.hint: About 25-30 miles of range per hour. This is what most people get and it is plenty for daily driving.

options.label: Fast — for a big battery or two cars
options.hint: About 40 miles of range per hour. Needs heavier wire and has to be wired in directly, not plugged in.

options.label: I don't know — recommend one
options.hint: We'll price the normal one. It suits almost everybody.

ask.question: How fast do you want it to charge?
ask.help: Faster charging costs more to install because it needs thicker wire and a bigger breaker — not because the charger costs more.
ask.why: This sets the size of the circuit, which sets the price of the wire and the breaker.

options.label: I've ordered one, it's not here yet
No — include one in the price

ask.question: Do you have the charger already?
ask.help: If you already have one, get it out of the box and check the next question — the answer is usually printed on it or in the first page of the manual.
ask.why: If we supply it, that's a real cost in the price. If you supply it, it isn't.

options.label: It has a plug on the end
options.hint: A big three-prong-plus-round plug, like an electric range. Called a 14-50.

options.label: It's wired in directly
options.hint: Wires go straight into the box, no plug.

ask.question: Does your charger plug in, or wire in directly?
ask.help: Look at the cable coming out of the back or bottom of the unit. A plug is unmistakable — it's chunky and has four pins.
ask.why: A plug-in charger needs a special safety breaker that costs about three times a normal one, because the code requires it for that kind of outlet. Wiring in directly avoids that. It's often the biggest surprise on an EV quote, so we'd rather tell you now.

options.label: Wire it in directly
options.hint: Cheaper, tidier, and what we'd suggest if the charger isn't going to move.

options.label: Put an outlet in and plug it in
options.hint: Costs more — a plug-in outlet for a charger needs a special safety breaker — but you can unplug the charger and take it with you.

ask.question: Since we're supplying it — plug it in, or wire it in?
ask.why: Wiring in is usually a couple of hundred dollars cheaper because of the breaker the code requires behind a plug.

states.explain: Turns the plain-English charging speed into a circuit size. Note the cap: a plug-in charger cannot be run above a 50A circuit, so choosing 'fast' AND 'plug in' quietly becomes a 50A circuit and the quote says so out loud.

NEC 625.54: a receptacle serving an EVSE has to be GFCI protected. A hardwired charger has that protection built in, so it does not. This one rule is worth roughly a hundred dollars of breaker and it is the line homeowners most often query.

Picks the wire. The rule that surprises people: 6-gauge romex is only rated 55A, so a 60A circuit cannot use it — it has to be individual conductors in conduit. That single code fact is the difference between a $3.40/ft job and a conduit job, and no homeowner has any way to know it.

Long runs lose voltage. The real number is a calculation, not a rule of thumb: at 240V a 32A continuous load on #8 copper stays inside 3% to roughly 145 feet, and a 48A load on #6 to roughly 150. So we set the trigger at a conservative 120 feet rather than repeating the common myth that anything over 50 feet needs upsizing — it does not, and charging for it would be dishonest.
The only place a terminal is chosen. Order matters and is the order of seriousness: safety, then capacity, then the normal job, then 'we haven't looked at your photo yet'.

conditions.say: We've priced this as a plug-in charger, which is the more expensive of the two. If yours wires in directly, we'll take about $150 off before you pay anything.

You asked for fast charging and a plug. Those two don't go together — a plug-in charger is limited to a 50A circuit. We've priced the fastest plug-in setup. If you want the full speed, we'd wire it in directly instead; say the word and we'll re-price it.
We'll look at your panel photo within a few hours and narrow this down. The top of the range won't move.
This price includes opening the wall and putting the wire in. It does not include making the wall look new again — see the patching option below.

terminals.title: A small extra panel, then your charger
terminals.summary: Your panel is out of spaces. The usual fix isn't a new service — it's a small second panel fed off the first one, which gives you room for the charger and a few spares for next time.
terminals.extends_note: Everything the standard install charges, plus the subpanel. Authored as an extension so a contractor who edits the run-labour maths edits it once.
includes_extra: A 100A subpanel mounted next to or near your existing one
A feeder from the main panel to it

line_items_extra.label: Feed breaker in the main panel

uncertainty.extra_spread_because: Where exactly the second panel can go is a judgement call we make on site.

conditions.say: We're suggesting this rather than a whole new service because your service size looks fine — you've just run out of room in the box. It's the cheaper answer and it leaves you space for the next thing.

terminals.title: Your charger, sharing power with the house
terminals.summary: Your panel has room, but your home's total electrical service is tight — a 100A service already running an electric range, dryer or heat pump doesn't have much left. Rather than upgrading the whole service, we fit a load-management device: it watches what the house is using and quietly slows the charger when everything's on at once. Overnight, you'd never notice.
includes_extra: A load-management module fitted at the panel
Setting it up and demonstrating it before we go

line_items_extra.label: Fitting and setting up the module

alternatives.label: Or upgrade the service instead
alternatives.copy: If you're planning a heat pump, a second car or an addition, it can be worth doing the bigger job once. Here's what that costs.

uncertainty.extra_spread_because: Until the load calculation is done we can't be certain this route is permitted in your jurisdiction.

conditions.say: This depends on a load calculation, which we do before we file the permit. If it comes back saying your service genuinely can't take it, we'll tell you before we order anything and you'll owe us nothing.

terminals.kind_note: Deliberately NOT a quote. This machine never collected the answers a service upgrade actually prices off — how many circuits come back, where the meter is, whether the service comes in overhead. Emitting a number here would be the machine pricing a job it did not ask about. It shows an indicative band, names the real machine, and books a visit.
terminals.title: Your service needs upgrading first
terminals.summary: Adding a charger to your home would draw more than your electrical service can safely supply. That's a bigger job than the charger: a new panel, a new meter enclosure, and your utility company involved.
terminals.handoff_note: Hands off to the service-upgrade machine, carrying the answers already collected so the homeowner is never asked the same thing twice. `composed_of` below is the shape a future combined quote would take once the handoff machine has run — it is not evaluated from here.
terminals.body: Adding a charger is the small half of this job. The big half is the service, and that one needs someone standing in front of your meter before anybody says a number.

conditions.say: We won't take a deposit on a job this size from a form. Someone comes out, confirms it, and then you decide.

There may be a cheaper way. If your panel has room and it's only the total that's tight, a load-management device can let you charge without upgrading anything. Ask us — we'd rather sell you the small job if it's the right one.

alternatives.label: Or share power instead of upgrading

terminals.title: Here's your range — we'll narrow it today
terminals.summary: Everything except your panel is clear. Until one of our electricians has read the photo, this range covers both possibilities: a straightforward job if there's room in the panel, and the bigger one if there isn't.
terminals.span_note: Not a wider version of one price — literally the cheapest outcome's low end to the most expensive outcome's high end. The homeowner is being shown the real shape of their uncertainty, not a padded guess.

resolution.promise: Within one business day, usually within a few hours.
resolution.narrowing_rule: Re-evaluation may only move the range INSIDE what was shown. If reading the photo reveals an outcome above this high end, we do not reprice silently — we call.

presentation.cta: Book the earliest slot — we'll confirm the price first
presentation.secondary_cta: Just send me the price when you know

conditions.say: If you send us a photo of your panel now, we can usually cut this range in half within the hour.
Your photo's with us. Nothing more needed from you.

refuse_to_quote_when.because: Past 150 feet the route matters more than the distance and we'd be guessing.
Cutting a driveway is a different trade with a price we can't guess from a form.
Aluminium branch wiring changes what we can connect to and has to be looked at.
Manufactured homes have a different kind of service equipment and the rules are different.
A 60A service can't take a charger on any reading. That's a service upgrade conversation, not a charger one.
